chunks.arabic_text: ظَفَرُ بْنُ حَمْدُونَ بْنِ شَدَّادٍ، الْبَادِرَائِيِّ، أَبُو مَنْصُورٍ. رَوَى عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْأَحْمَرِيِّ.

translations.en: Ẓafar ibn Ḥamdūn ibn Shaddād, al-Bādirā’ī, Abū Manṣūr. He narrated from Ibrāhīm al-Aḥmarī.
There was weakness in his madhhab.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Duafa* highlights Ẓafar ibn Ḥamdūn al-Bādirā’ī, noting a specific weakness in his *madhhab* (doctrinal stance or school of thought) rather than mere memory precision, which is a key distinction in Shia rijal sciences. This type of doctrinal nuance often reflects sectarian alignments or theological deviations that affect the acceptance of his narrations within the Imami tradition. Such entries underscore the scholarly rigor applied to evaluating not just the chain of transmission, but the intellectual and theological reliability of the narrator.
en.seo_question: Who is Ẓafar ibn Ḥamdūn al-Bādirā’ī and what is the assessment of his madhhab?

key_terms.مَذْهَب: School of thought or doctrinal stance
